label: mainresult
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{mainresult}
Every Besicovitch set in $\mathbb{R}^4$ has Hausdorff dimension at least $\frac{13}{4}-\frac{12951-54\sqrt{10593}}{41972}=3.073854...$.

title: Definition
body_md: A $\delta$-tube is the $\delta$-neighborhood of a unit line segment in $\mathbb{R}^4$. Every $\delta$-tube has measure $\sim\delta^3$. We say that two $\delta$-tubes are essentially identical if the 2-fold dilate of one of the tubes contains the other. If two tubes are not essentially identical then we say they are essentially distinct.
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md: A $\delta$-cube is a set of the form $Q=[0,\delta)^4+v$, where $v\in (\delta\mathbb{Z})^4$. Observe that the set of all $\delta$-cubes tile $\mathbb{R}^4$. The symbol $Q$ will always refer to a $\delta$-cube, so for example the expression $\sum_{Q\subset A}f(Q)$ will refer to a sum taken over all $\delta$-cubes contained in the set $A$.
head: environment

label: shading
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{shading}
Let $T$ be a $\delta$-tube. A shading of $T$ is a set $Y(T)$ that is a union of $\delta$-cubes, each of which intersect $T$. Let $\mathbb{T}$ be a set of $\delta$-tubes; for each $T\in\mathbb{T}$, let $Y(T)$ be a shading of $T$. We refer to the pair $(\mathbb{T},Y)$ as a set of tubes and their associated shading.

label: grdecomp
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{grdecomp} (Graphical decomposition)
    Let $P\in \mathbb{R}[x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4]$ be a non-zero polynomial of degree at most $d$, and let $Z=Z(P)\cap [-1,1]^4$. Then there exists $N, C\lesssim_d 1$, and $v_n \in \{e_1,e_2,e_3,e_4\}$ for $1\leq n \leq N$, and connected smooth semi-algebraic manifolds $S_n\subset Z$; such that
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
        \item we have $Z=\bigcup_{n=1}^N S_n$.
        \item each $S_n$ has complexity at most $C$.
        \item for all $p\in S_n$, we have $\operatorname{proj}_{N_p S_n}(v_n)\geq 1/2$.
        \item if $\pi_n:\mathbb{R}^4\to v_n^\perp$ denotes the orthogonal projection, then $S_n$ is a graph in the $v_n$ direction of a function with Lipschitz constant at most $C$.
        \item the set $S_{n,\delta}=N_\delta(S_n)$ is semi-algebraic of complexity at most $C$ (uniformly in $\delta$), and
        \begin{equation}
            \mathcal{H}^1 (S_{n,\delta}\cap \pi_n^{-1}(y))\leq C\delta
        \end{equation}
        for all $y\in v_n^\perp$.
    \end{enumerate}

title: Definition

A grain (of complexity $d$) in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is the $C\delta$--neighborhood of a semi-algebraic set of dimension $\leq n-1$ and complexity $\leq d$.

title: Definition
body_md: Let $(\mathbb{T},Y)$ be a set of $\delta$-tubes and their associated shading. We say that $(\mathbb{T},Y)$ is plany if for each $\delta$-cube $Q$, there is a plane $\Pi(Q)$ so that for all $T\in\mathbb{T}_Y(Q)$ we have $\angle(v(T),\Pi(Q))\lesssim\delta$.

label: planyOrTrilinearLem
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{planyOrTrilinearLem}
Let $(\mathbb{T},Y)$ be a set of $\delta$-tubes and their associated shading. Suppose that $(\mathbb{T},Y)$ is $(\epsilon_1,C_1)$-two-ends and $(\epsilon_2,C_2)$-robustly transverse.

Then there exists a number $\delta\leq\theta\leq 1$; a refinement $(\mathbb{T}^\prime,Y^\prime)$ of $(\mathbb{T},Y)$; a set $\Omega\subset S^3$ of $\theta$-separated points; a set $(\mathbb{T}_{\theta},Y_\theta)$ of essentially distinct $\theta$-tubes and their associated shading; and numbers $B,B_1,B_2\geq 1$ with $B_1\geq B_2$ and $B_1/B_2 \leq B$ so that the following holds.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item\label{deltaCubePlane} For each $Q\in\mathcal{Q}(Y^\prime)$, there is a plane $\Pi(Q)$ so that $\angle(v(T),\Pi(Q))\leq\theta$ for all $T\in\mathbb{T}_Y(Q)$.

\item\label{mostTriplesWedgeThetaItem} For each $Q\in\mathcal{Q}(Y^\prime)$,
\begin{equation}\label{mostTriplesWedgeTheta}
|\{T_1,T_2,T_3\in \mathbb{T}_{Y^\prime}(Q)\colon |v(T_1)\wedge v(T_2)\wedge v(T_3)|\gtrsim \theta\}|\gtrapprox|\mathbb{T}_{Y^\prime}(Q)|^3.
\end{equation}

\item\label{directionsThetaTubes} Every tube in $\mathbb{T}_\theta$ points in a direction from $\Omega$. For each $v\in\Omega$, there are $\sim|\mathbb{T}_\theta|/|\Omega|$ tubes from $\mathbb{T}_\theta$ that point in direction $v$.

\item\label{thinTubesInsideThetaTubes} Each tube $T_\theta \in\mathbb{T}_\theta$ contains $\sim |\mathbb{T}^\prime|/|\mathbb{T}_\theta|$ tubes from $\mathbb{T}^\prime$, and each tube from $\mathbb{T}^\prime$ is contained in exactly one tube from $\mathbb{T}_\theta$.

\item\label{fineShadingInsideCourseShading} If $T\in\mathbb{T}, T_\theta\in\mathbb{T}_\theta$, and $T\subset T_\theta$, then $Y^\prime(T)\subset Y_\theta(T_\theta)$.

\item\label{lowerBoundLambdaYTheta} $\lambda_{Y_\theta}\gtrapprox \lambda_{Y^\prime}$. 

\item\label{thetaTubesAreTwoEnds} $(\mathbb{T}_\theta,Y_\theta)$ is $(\varepsilon_1,C_1^\prime)$-two-ends, with $C_1^\prime\lessapprox 1$.

\item\label{tubesHaveUniformMult} For each $\delta$-cube $Q\in\mathcal{Q}(Y)$, we have $|\mathbb{T}_{Y^\prime}(Q)|\sim \mu_{Y^\prime}$. For each $\theta$-cube $Q\in\mathcal{Q}(Y_\theta)$ we have $|\mathbb{T}_{\theta}(Q)|\sim \mu_{Y_\theta}$.

\item\label{innerTubesHaveUniformMult} There is a number $\mu_{\operatorname{fine}}$ so that for each $T_\theta\in\mathbb{T}_{\theta}$, we have $\mu_{Y_{T_\theta}}\sim\mu_{\operatorname{fine}}$. 

\item\label{thetaTubesInPlanes} For each $\theta$-cube $Q_\theta\in\mathcal{Q}(Y_\theta)$, there are planes $\Pi_1(Q_\theta),\ldots,\Pi_{B_1}(Q_\theta)$ and collections of tubes $\mathbb{T}_{1,\theta}(Q_\theta),\ldots,\mathbb{T}_{B_1,\theta} \subset\mathbb{T}_\theta(Q_\theta)$ so that for each index $i$, the tubes in $\mathbb{T}_{i,\theta}(Q_\theta)$ satisfy $\angle(T_\theta,\Pi_i(Q_\theta))\leq\theta$ and $|\mathbb{T}_{i,\theta}|=\mu_{Y_\theta}/B$. Each tube $T\in\mathbb{T}_{\theta}(Q)$ is contained in $B_2$ of sets $\{\mathbb{T}_{i,\theta}(Q_\theta)\}.$ 

\item\label{productMultiplicity} We have the multiplicity bound
\begin{equation*}
\mu_{Y^\prime}\lessapprox \mu_{Y_{\theta}}\mu_{\operatorname{fine}}/B.
\end{equation*}


\end{enumerate}
